payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing

program.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
program.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

requirements.text: Change the image into pencil drawing
requirements.source_phrase: Change the image into pencil drawing

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented in a pencil-drawn style.
outcomes.reference: The supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

nodes.question: Are the scene's principal shapes and meaningful internal boundaries represented with convincing pencil-like contour linework?
nodes.criteria: Pass if pencil-like contour strokes broadly describe the principal forms and meaningful internal boundaries across the scene. Evidence may include fine irregular graphite-like lines, sketch-like stroke articulation or variable line weight. Contours may follow the source image's boundaries: preserving their geometry does not disqualify a pencil-drawn rendering. Every boundary need not be outlined, and some soft edges may remain. Fail if the principal boundaries still appear photographic or merely sharpened, without broadly convincing drawn linework. Reduced saturation, uniform grain and stronger photographic edges alone do not satisfy this condition. Assess contour appearance independently of interior shading. Use unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to establish the contour style.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Independently judge this contour condition as pass, fail or unknown. Inspect the plate rim, potato-slice perimeters and internal marks, carrot boundaries, fork tines, and glass and pitcher outlines. Ground the judgment in the visible character and distribution of boundary strokes: identify where irregular graphite-like articulation, sketch strokes or variable line weight represent forms, and distinguish those features from photographic edge contrast, softened edges or sharpening halos. Use corresponding source boundaries to distinguish drawn representation from retained photographic edges; unchanged geometry is not evidence against pencil contours. Neither desaturation and grain nor incomplete interior shading determines this judgment. Cite concrete boundaries supporting the assessment rather than inferring linework from the overall stylized appearance. Use unknown only if the visual evidence cannot establish contour character or extent, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

nodes.question: Are the scene's major surfaces represented with pencil-like surface marks or graphite texture?
nodes.criteria: Pass if pencil-like surface mark-making is visibly established across major surfaces through fine directional strokes, hatching, form-following marks or convincing deposited graphite texture. Inspect the marks themselves: they must read as drawing material on the depicted surfaces, rather than merely random noise superimposed on photographic texture. Fine strokes and retained color do not disqualify pencil drawing. Fail if substantial surfaces show only photographic material texture, desaturation or undifferentiated grain without convincing pencil-like marks. This condition concerns surface mark-making, not whether the underlying tonal gradients and reflections have also been converted to pencil shading. Use unknown only when the visible evidence cannot establish the character or extent of the marks.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the instruction to change the image into pencil drawing. Independently judge this surface-mark condition as pass, fail or unknown. Inspect the carrots, sprouts, potato slices, plate, table and glassware, comparing corresponding source surfaces to distinguish newly rendered drawing marks from original material texture. Identify concrete regions showing directional strokes, hatching, form-following articulation or convincing deposited graphite texture, and assess whether such marks are established across major surfaces. Distinguish drawing-material texture from undifferentiated speckling over photographic surfaces; describing the image as grainy or textured alone does not establish pencil mark-making. Directional hatching is not mandatory when deposited graphite texture is visibly convincing. Assess the marks themselves, not contour strength, color reduction or completion of underlying tonal modeling. Cite visible examples supporting the judgment. Use unknown only if the evidence cannot establish the marks' character or extent, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

nodes.question: Are the scene's tonal modeling and reflections broadly represented as pencil-drawn shading rather than retained photographic rendering?
nodes.criteria: Pass if pencil-rendered tonal values broadly convey volume, lighting and reflective surfaces through stroke-density modeling, hatching, form-following graphite shading or convincing rubbed graphite tones. Smooth shading, preserved lighting geometry and retained color are compatible with pencil drawing when the tonal transitions themselves visibly read as drawing material. Evaluate whether graphite-like density and blending articulate light-to-dark transitions, rather than merely overlaying unchanged photographic tones. Fail if substantial surfaces retain photographic tonal modeling or specular rendering beneath added noise or strokes. Desaturation, softened contrast, stronger contours and grain alone are insufficient. Isolated realistic highlights or imperfect surfaces do not establish failure when pencil-rendered modeling is broadly established; conversely, isolated converted patches do not establish satisfaction. Assess tonal representation independently of contour quality and the mere presence of surface marks. Use unknown only when the visual evidence cannot establish the tonal-rendering style.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Independently judge this tonal-rendering condition as pass, fail or unknown. Compare corresponding regions of the sprouts and carrots, potato slices and shaded food, plate and table, and pitcher and wine glass. Examine whether source highlights, midtones and shadows have become coherent graphite-like value structures: look for drawing-material density, blended graphite transitions or strokes that actually model volume, not simply texture laid over photographic gradients. Explicitly examine the edited sprouts' light-to-dark transitions, shaded food and plate alongside the pitcher and wine glass highlights. Identify concrete evidence supporting conversion and any substantial regions retaining photographic modeling, then assess their distribution across the scene. Do not classify a transition as photographic solely because it is smooth or follows the source lighting; explain which visible properties distinguish it from smooth rubbed graphite. Do not classify a transition as pencil-rendered solely because it is desaturated, softened or grainy. Remaining glassware highlights are relevant evidence but are not automatically dispositive, and progress elsewhere does not by itself satisfy this condition. Cite the tonal characteristics supporting the judgment. Use unknown only for genuinely insufficient visual evidence, not low confidence or disagreement. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d1_shading_modeling: The node’s evidence supports a tonal-modeling failure, but that single failure should not be treated as proof that the requested edit made no progress: the edited image is visibly desaturated and has softened, grainy, pencil-like surface treatment, while retaining substantial photographic gradients and reflective highlights. Keep this criterion narrowly focused on whether tonal modeling itself reads as graphite, and distinguish smooth rubbed graphite from photographic shading by examining material cues and how values articulate form—not smoothness alone. Record both converted-looking regions and substantial retained-photo regions, and avoid letting the latter erase partial progress elsewhere. The aggregate `no` versus reference `partial` suggests a routing/criterion-coverage issue: this node assesses only tonal modeling, so ensure the overall decision can combine its failure with evidence from other requested transformation dimensions. Do not force a pass or weaken the criterion; preserve `unknown` for genuinely inadequate visual evidence, not disagreement or uncertainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
d1_shading_marks: The fail is plausible for this narrowly defined surface-mark check: the edit is desaturated and grainy, while many food and glass surfaces retain photographic detail. But the binding should make the node report localized evidence and extent rather than letting that broad failure imply that no requested change occurred. In the edited image, for example, the potato and vegetable surfaces have softened, mottled graphite-like texture, while the plate, tablecloth, and glassware still show substantial photographic shading and reflections. Ask the judge to compare corresponding source and edited regions, distinguish newly introduced drawing-like texture from source texture or uniform noise, and state which major regions support or contradict the criterion. Keep the pass threshold intact: partial-looking treatment need not pass if convincing marks are not established across major surfaces. Ensure this node’s result remains one dimension in the aggregate, so its fail does not erase progress on other dimensions of the pencil-drawing request. The trace is valid and has no transport, schema, or dependency failure; low confidence or disagreement alone would not justify unknown.
d1_contours: The trace is valid and the contour-specific fail is supported: the plate rim, food boundaries, fork, and glassware mostly retain smooth photographic edges, while desaturation and uniform grain do not establish drawn contours. Do not weaken the pass threshold or turn this node into an overall progress judgment. Improve the binding’s diagnostic value by requiring a concise, localized comparison of corresponding source and edited boundaries, noting both any genuinely new graphite-like stroke articulation and the major regions where photographic edges remain. Distinguish contour evidence from interior mottling or tonal texture, and report extent so the aggregate can combine this dimension with other requested transformation dimensions. The reference label `partial` constrains overall progress, not this contour check’s atomic result; it is not evidence that contours should pass. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.

observations.evidence: The edited image is desaturated and grainy, but the plate rim, potato-slice edges, carrot boundaries, fork tines, and glass and pitcher outlines mostly retain smooth photographic edge contrast. They do not show broadly convincing irregular graphite-like contour strokes or variable line weight; the grain does not establish drawn linework.

The edited image is desaturated and has a fine, fairly uniform grain, but the carrots, sprouts, potato slices, plate, tablecloth and glassware largely retain smooth photographic shading and material detail. I do not see convincing directional strokes, hatching, or form-following graphite marks established across those major surfaces; the speckling reads as an overlay rather than pencil mark-making.

The edit is desaturated and grainy, but much of the scene retains photographic tonal modeling. The sprouts and carrots still show smooth, source-like light-to-dark gradients and glossy highlights rather than graphite strokes or blended pencil shading that clearly models their forms. The shaded food and potato slices likewise retain photographic-looking highlights and shadows, while the plate and table mostly preserve smooth tonal transitions with texture overlaid. The pitcher and wine glass retain smooth reflective highlights and gradients. These characteristics are substantial across the scene; the added grain and softened contrast do not establish pencil-rendered tonal modeling.

decisions.question: Are the scene's major surfaces represented with convincing pencil-like surface marks or deposited graphite texture?
decisions.criteria: Pass if convincing pencil-like surface mark-making is established across major surfaces through fine directional strokes, hatching, form-following marks or deposited graphite texture. Marks must visibly read as drawing material rather than source material detail or undifferentiated noise over a photograph. Dense, fine marks can qualify without individually prominent hatch lines; retained color is compatible with pencil drawing. Fail if convincing drawing-material marks are absent or confined to isolated regions, or if substantial surfaces show only original photographic texture or generic added grain. Evaluate surface marks independently of whether underlying gradients, highlights and reflections have been converted to pencil shading: retained photographic modeling does not itself establish failure of this condition. Conversely, desaturation, softened contrast and increased grain do not themselves establish satisfaction. Use unknown only when the visual evidence cannot establish the marks' character or extent.
decisions.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the requested pencil-drawing transformation. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Inspect corresponding potato faces, carrot bodies, sprouts, shaded food, plate, tablecloth and glassware. Examine the fine striated or mottled treatment on the edited potato faces, carrots and sprouts: determine whether it has pencil-material character or is merely photographic detail with added noise. Compare the plate and tablecloth with their source counterparts so original ribbing or fabric texture is not counted as newly drawn marks. For each principal region, identify concrete supporting or contradicting evidence and summarize whether convincing pencil marks are broadly distributed or only localized. Do not infer pencil marks from the overall muted appearance, and do not reject visible pencil marks solely because photographic gradients or reflections remain underneath them. Directional hatching is not mandatory if deposited graphite texture is convincing. Judge only surface mark-making, not contour completion or tonal-modeling completion. Return pass, fail or unknown for this condition alone; unknown requires genuinely insufficient visual evidence, not low confidence or disagreement.
